headline: BLACK HOLE now falls through its own horizon
lede: The flyby loop ends in a real radial plunge: the outside universe compresses into a shrinking escape cone, Doppler-beamed D^3 and blueshifted into a bright circle, while the hole's shadow takes the whole frame — then the dark interior fades back to the start.

notes.text: Plunge camera: r(s) free-fall profile crossing r=rs with a smooth tip-over, horizon crossing with no flash (physics, not a fade trick), and a loop-restart that clears dropped probes.

Fixed a latent GR bug: the tracer treated Euclidean screen angles as local ones; near the horizon b = r·sinψ/√(1−rs/r) diverges. Launcher rebuilt in the shader and both JS mirrors; photon ring gated outside the photon sphere.

blackholecheck 59 -> 75 gates: escape-cone formula match, monotone dive radius, blueshift rise, cone-to-zero at the horizon, mostly-dark-frame + bright blue-white core pixel gate, loop auto-restart, and a fifth proven-fail mutant (pin the beaming uniform -> pixel gate red, physics green).
Rebased mid-flight onto QA's #1074 probe polish (puff, trail, Doppler hue, rim-fade) — probe visuals now ride the loop fade.

look.text: Watch a full loop — flyby, tap to drop probes, then the plunge
